chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskan from Abdul Malik ibn Amr, that he asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):

About performing Tamattu' with Umrah until Hajj, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Perform Tamattu'.' He said, 'So it happened that he (peace be upon him) performed the exclusive Hajj in that year or after it, so I said, 'May Allah keep you well! I asked you and you instructed me with Tamattu', and I see you to have performed the exclusive Hajj this year?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'But, by Allah, the merit is in that which I had instructed you with, but I am (physically) weak, so it was difficult upon me, the two circumambulations between Al-Safa and Al-Marwa, therefore, due to that, I performed the exclusive Hajj'.

key_terms.التَّمَتُّعُ: Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj with a break in between)
key_terms.الصَّفَا: Al-Safa (one of the two hills between which Sa'i is performed)
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: Al-Marwa (the second hill in the Sa'i ritual)
key_terms.طَوَافَانِ: Two circumambulations (referring to the Sa'i ritual performed twice in Tamattu')

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Tamattu' Hajj and why did the Imam perform exclusive Hajj if he recommended Tamattu'?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the practical flexibility within Shia jurisprudence, illustrating that the Imam’s personal choice to perform Qiran (or exclusive Hajj) due to physical weakness does not negate the merit of Tamattu'. It underscores the principle that while Tamattu' is highly recommended, the validity of other forms of Hajj remains intact when necessitated by individual circumstances, reflecting the balance between ideal religious practice and human capacity.
